page.title: PhD Math Camp
page.subtitle: Interactive companions to the math camp lectures
page.description: A short, intensive review of the mathematics used in graduate political science methods. The units below follow the lecture sequence, and each one links to its slides. Where a unit also has interactive material, its figures are reproduced as live Desmos graphs with the parameters left free, so they can be moved during class.

note.title: How these are built
note.body: The graphs are generated from a single Python script using SymPy for the algebra, SciPy and NumPy to check the numerical results, and PyDesmos to emit the Desmos expressions. Nothing is drawn by hand, so the curves and the labelled roots are exactly what the symbolic solver returns.

units.title: Intro, Logic and Sets
units.description: Propositional and predicate logic, set operations, and applications to social science.

units.title: Relations and Functions
units.description: Relations, the vertical-line test, composition and inverses, polynomial roots, logarithms and exponentials, and monotonicity.

graphs.title: A relation that is not a function
graphs.description: Drag the slider to sweep a vertical line across the sideways parabola. It meets the curve twice for every x > 0, which is exactly what disqualifies the relation from being a function.

graphs.title: Many-to-one vs one-to-one
graphs.description: The horizontal-line test. Sweeping y = c meets the parabola twice but the line once, separating the many-to-one map from the one-to-one map.

graphs.title: Functions from ℝ to ℝ
graphs.description: The five examples from the Dimensions slide on one set of axes, for comparing growth and shape.

graphs.title: Function composition
graphs.description: Desmos composes the two functions live. The slider traces a single input through both stages, t → f(t) → g(f(t)), so the nesting is visible as two hops rather than one formula.

graphs.title: Inverse functions
graphs.description: Each function is plotted with its inverse and the line y = x. The inverses are obtained symbolically rather than typed in, and the reflection across the diagonal is the point of the picture.

graphs.title: Roots of a polynomial
graphs.description: Expanded and factored forms drawn on top of each other, with the three roots marked. The roots are found symbolically and re-checked numerically with a bracketing solver.

graphs.title: The quadratic formula
graphs.description: Sliders for a, b and c, with the discriminant and both roots entered as expressions. Moving c until the discriminant goes negative makes the root markers disappear, which is the useful thing to show.

graphs.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
graphs.description: The reflection pair. The slider carries a point on the exponential to its mirror image on the logarithm, across y = x.

graphs.title: Monotonic functions
graphs.description: Both functions with their derivatives dotted underneath. The constant derivative and the sign change at the origin are what distinguish the monotonic case from the non-monotonic one.

graphs.title: Functions from ℝ² to ℝ
graphs.expression: x² + y² = k, 2x + y = k, x³ + 2y² = k
graphs.description: The surfaces from the slides seen from above. Desmos graphs in two dimensions, so each surface appears as its level sets, and the slider on k moves the cutting plane up and down.

units.title: Limits and Continuity
units.description: Sequences and their limits, the limit of a function, and continuity.

units.title: Calculus — Derivatives
units.description: The derivative, rules of differentiation, optimization, and finding extrema in one dimension.

units.title: Calculus — Integrals
units.description: Integration motivated through probability: sample spaces and random variables, discrete versus continuous distributions, the relationship between the density and the CDF, and Riemann sums as approximations of area.

units.title: Linear Algebra
units.description: Vectors and vector operations, orthogonality, span, basis and linear independence, systems of equations, matrix operations, and an introduction to multivariate calculus.
